sentences.text: Empress Matilda -LRB- c. 7 February 110210 September 1167 -RRB- , also known as the Empress Maude , was the claimant to the English throne during the civil war known as the Anarchy .	the Anarchy	the Anarchy

The daughter of King Henry I of England , she moved to Germany as a child when she married the future Holy Roman Emperor Henry V .	Henry I of England	Henry I of England	King Henry I of England	Henry I of England	Holy Roman Emperor Henry V	Henry V, Holy Roman Emperor
She travelled with her husband into Italy in 1116 , was controversially crowned in St. Peter 's Basilica , and acted as the imperial regent in Italy .	regent	regent
Matilda and Henry had no children , and when Henry died in 1125 , the crown was claimed by Lothair II , one of his political enemies .	Lothair II	Lothair II, Holy Roman Emperor

Meanwhile , Matilda 's younger brother , William Adelin , died in the White Ship disaster of 1120 , leaving England facing a potential succession crisis .	William Adelin	William Adelin	White Ship	White Ship

On Henry V 's death , Matilda was recalled to Normandy by her father , who arranged for her to marry Geoffrey of Anjou to form an alliance to protect his southern borders .	Normandy	Duchy of Normandy	Geoffrey of Anjou	Geoffrey Plantagenet, Count of Anjou

Henry I had no further legitimate children and nominated Matilda as his heir , making his court swear an oath of loyalty to her and her successors , but the decision was not popular in the Anglo-Norman court .	Anglo-Norman	Anglo-Norman	oath	oath
Henry died in 1135 but Matilda and Geoffrey faced opposition from the Norman barons and were unable to pursue their claims .

The throne was instead taken by Matilda 's cousin Stephen of Blois , who enjoyed the backing of the English Church .	Stephen	Stephen, King of England	Stephen of Blois	Stephen, King of England	English Church	Christianity in England
Stephen took steps to solidify his new regime , but faced threats both from neighbouring powers and from opponents within his kingdom .	Stephen	Stephen, King of England

In 1139 Matilda crossed to England to take the kingdom by force , supported by her half-brother , Robert of Gloucester , and her uncle , King David I of Scotland , while Geoffrey focused on conquering Normandy .	Normandy	Duchy of Normandy	Robert of Gloucester	Robert, 1st Earl of Gloucester	King David I of Scotland	David I of Scotland

Matilda 's forces captured Stephen at the Battle of Lincoln in 1141 , but the Empress 's attempt to be crowned at Westminster collapsed in the face of bitter opposition from the London crowds .	Stephen	Stephen, King of England	Battle of Lincoln	Battle of Lincoln (1141)	Westminster	Westminster Abbey
As a result of this retreat , Matilda was never formally declared Queen of England , and was instead titled the Lady of the English .	Lady of the English	List of English monarchs
Robert was captured following the Rout of Winchester in 1141 , and Matilda agreed to exchange him for Stephen .	Stephen	Stephen, King of England	Rout of Winchester	Rout of Winchester

Matilda became trapped in Oxford Castle by Stephen 's forces that winter , and was forced to escape across the frozen River Isis at night to avoid capture .	Stephen	Stephen, King of England	Oxford Castle	Oxford Castle	River Isis	River Isis
The war degenerated into a stalemate , with Matilda controlling much of the south-west of England , and Stephen the south-east and the Midlands .	Stephen	Stephen, King of England
Large parts of the rest of the country were in the hands of local , independent barons .

Matilda returned to Normandy , now in the hands of her husband , in 1148 , leaving her eldest son to continue the campaign in England ; he eventually succeeded to the throne as Henry II in 1154 .	Normandy	Duchy of Normandy	Henry II	Henry II of England
She settled her court near Rouen and for the rest of her life concerned herself with the administration of Normandy , acting on Henry 's behalf when necessary .	Normandy	Duchy of Normandy	Rouen	Rouen
Particularly in the early years of her son 's reign , she provided political advice and attempted to mediate during the Becket controversy .	Becket controversy	Becket controversy
She worked extensively with the Church , founding Cistercian monasteries , and was known for her piety .	Cistercian	Cistercian
She was buried under the high altar at Bec Abbey after her death in 1167 .	Bec Abbey	Bec Abbey
